hero.title: Collect the record
hero.text: Design the collect → protect → analyze pipeline, then build its first stage: audit policy on the DCs and admin hosts, and SBD-SYSLOG01 receiving Windows events by subscription and syslog from the router and SBD-REPO01. Follow the build, explore the dependencies, and keep the evidence.

sample: SBD-DC01 · SBD-DC02 · SBD-SUBCA01 · SBD-PKI-MGMT01 · SBD-DHCP01 · admin seats VLAN 60 · SBD-REPO01 10.0.70.20
F17 WinRM 5985 · F07 syslog TLS 6514 · F24 router deny log UDP 514 · F11 SMB 445 · F10 TCP 9997

scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing the domain controllers, the PKI and DHCP servers, the administration hosts, the core router, and SBD-REPO01 sending their records to the collector SBD-SYSLOG01.
scene.completeCaption: Every existing source pushes its record to SBD-SYSLOG01: Windows events by subscription, the router's denies and SBD-REPO01's messages as syslog. Courses 1.11 and 1.12 pick up the two streams from here.

nodes.name: SBD-SYSLOG01
nodes.title: SBD-SYSLOG01 · 10.0.20.20
nodes.description: The collector this course builds. A source-initiated subscription fills ForwardedEvents, and its syslog receiver takes the router's denies on UDP 514 (F24) and Linux senders over TLS on TCP 6514. It reaches into no source.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: Built in course 1.1. Lesson 2 reconciles its audit policy with the course 1.5 STIG GPOs, lesson 3 enrolls it as a source, and lesson 5 traces a failed sign-in from it.

nodes.name: SBD-DC02
nodes.title: SBD-DC02 · 10.0.10.11
nodes.description: Built in course 1.1 and audited by the same GPOs as SBD-DC01. Its forwarded events keep the MachineName SBD-DC02, which is how the central copy shows where each record came from.

nodes.name: SBD-REPO01
nodes.title: SBD-REPO01 · 10.0.70.20
nodes.description: Built in course 1.9. In lesson 5 it becomes the first Linux source, forwarding its syslog over TLS to the collector on TCP 6514 (rule F07).

nodes.name: PKI + DHCP
nodes.title: SBD-SUBCA01 · SBD-PKI-MGMT01 · SBD-DHCP01
nodes.description: SBD-SUBCA01 and SBD-PKI-MGMT01 from course 1.6 and SBD-DHCP01 from course 1.7. Lesson 3 adds them to SBD Event Sources, so their Security logs and time events reach the collector like the controllers'.

nodes.name: ADMIN HOSTS
nodes.title: Admin hosts · 10.0.60.0/24
nodes.description: AdminJumpBox01, SBD-ADMIN-SRV01, and SBD-ADMIN-PC01 from course 1.8. Their sign-in events join the first collection scope, and SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 is where the collector is administered from.

stepTitles: Write each host's role and building course
Scope the first collection
Decide retention, readers, and the no-delete rule
Name the streams and their pickup folders
Add the pipeline's register rows
design.mistake: Letting the analysis system double as the archive. If SBD-SPLUNK01 held the only copy, anyone who can change its indexes or searches could change the evidence, and the AU-9 protection story would have nothing to stand on. Keep one copy to keep and one copy to question.
design.network: Only the design exists: SBD-SYSLOG01 is planned on VLAN 20. The domain controllers, PKI and DHCP servers, admin hosts, core router, and SBD-REPO01 already run, but no events flow yet. SBD-AUDIT01 and SBD-SPLUNK01 arrive in courses 1.11 and 1.12.

control.name: Audit Record Retention
control.body: Decide retention per stage before any record exists. The collector's buffer, the repository's protected copy, and the analysis copy have different clocks. Each period depends on your environment and policy: write down the one you chose and why, with the people who may read that stage.
control.question: How long must the protected copy outlive the working copy, and who made that decision?

checklist: I wrote the role sentence and building course for the collector, the repository, and the analysis system.
I recorded retention, readers, and the no-delete rule for each stage, and named the two streams and their pickup folders.
I added the five pipeline paths to the register with their owners, F24 for the router's deny log included.

stepTitles: Review what the course 1.5 STIG GPOs already audit
Confirm the design's subcategories on the DCs
Extend the policy to the Admin sub-OUs
Make every addition a documented GPO change
auditing.mistake: Filling a gap with auditpol /set on one server. Group Policy can overwrite the local change, it disappears when the server is rebuilt, and nobody reading the GPO report knows it was there. Make additions in the GPO structure and record them.
auditing.network: The domain controllers on VLAN 10 and the admin hosts on VLAN 60 now write the designed event families to their own Security logs. Nothing is forwarded yet; the collector is still planned.

control.name: Audit Record Generation
control.body: Records are generated on the source. Applying the designed subcategories through GPO, at or above the STIG values, makes the domain controllers and admin hosts write the records the design scoped, and keeps that setting visible in every GPO report.
control.question: If an event family were missing from a host's effective policy, how would you find out before you needed that record?

checklist: I captured the auditpol output for the domain controllers and the admin hosts.
I confirmed the designed subcategories are at or above the STIG values and applied through GPO.
I recorded every audit addition in its own GPO and in the exception record.

stepTitles: Enable the collector and create the subscription
Enroll the sources by one filtered GPO
Scope WinRM to the enrolled sources
Stand up the syslog intake
Confirm only registered paths are in use
collector.mistake: Forgetting NETWORK SERVICE in Event Log Readers, or not restarting the source after adding it. The subscription still shows the source as active, but no Security events reach ForwardedEvents, so the pipeline looks configured while carrying nothing.
collector.network: SBD-SYSLOG01 on VLAN 20 is online. Both domain controllers, the PKI and DHCP servers, and the admin hosts push events to it over WinRM 5985 (F17), and the core router's deny log arrives as syslog on UDP 514 (F24).

control.name: Content of Audit Records
control.body: A central copy is useful only if each record still says what happened, when, where, and to whom. Forwarded events keep their source machine name and time, so every record on the collector traces back to the host that wrote it.
control.question: Which fields on a forwarded event would you rely on to show an assessor where and when it happened?

checklist: I confirmed the subscription is enabled and the sources are enrolled by GPO.
I found forwarded Security and Time-Service events from every member of SBD Event Sources, each with its own MachineName.
I received a router deny entry in the syslog files and saw only the registered ports listening.

stepTitles: Read runtime status and find silent sources
Size the log and set its overwrite behavior
Check the disk and the syslog intake
Write the collection failure response
collector-health.mistake: Setting ForwardedEvents to retain events when full because keeping everything sounds safer. When the log fills, new events are refused, so the newest record is the one lost. Size the buffer past the pickup window and let it overwrite the oldest.
collector-health.network: The same flows run into SBD-SYSLOG01. This lesson watches them from the collector's side: each source's heartbeat, the log's oldest event, the data volume, and each syslog sender's daily file.

control.name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
control.body: A logging failure must reach a named person who acts. The written failure conditions, the logging owner who is told the same day, and the recorded gap window turn a silent stop into an event with a response.
control.question: If SBD-DC02 went silent on Friday evening, when would someone know, and what would they write down?

checklist: I confirmed every enrolled source is active with a recent heartbeat.
I set ForwardedEvents to overwrite oldest-first and confirmed it holds more than the buffer period I chose.
I wrote the failure conditions and the owner who is told, and kept the first daily check.

stepTitles: Trace one failed sign-in to the collector
Trace a router deny the same way
Enroll SBD-REPO01 over syslog TLS
Baseline the collector and rescan the DCs
Write the handoff to course 1.11
collector-prove.mistake: Typing the wrong password again and again. One failed sign-in is the test; a burst of failures can reach the domain's lockout threshold, lock a tier admin account the lab still needs, and bury the test event among others. Generate one event, then trace it.
collector-prove.network: Every source is live: the Windows sources forward over WinRM, the core router sends its denies on UDP 514 (F24), and SBD-REPO01 joins over syslog TLS on TCP 6514. One sign-in, one deny, and one test message reach SBD-SYSLOG01.

control.name: Time Stamps
control.body: A traced event is evidence only if its time agrees at every stop. Comparing the source's time with the collector's for a sign-in, a deny, and a Linux message shows the course 1.3 time design holding across Windows, the router, and Linux.
control.question: If the router's deny line were an hour off from the forwarded events, which system would you check first, and why?

checklist: I traced one failed sign-in and one router deny to the collector with matching source names and times.
I enrolled SBD-REPO01 over syslog TLS and found its test message on the collector.
I filed SBD-SYSLOG01's baseline, the DC rescan deltas, and the handoff to course 1.11.
